evidence.excerpt:
Long-horizon research agents solve open-
ended tasks through iterative retrieval, aggrega-
tion, and synthesis, but context grows rapidly
while the marginal value of additional evidence
often declines. This leads to unnecessary to-
ken costs, higher latency, and noisier inputs
for final report generation. We studymarginal
value estimationfor context management in a
GPT-Researcher-style deep research pipeline,
comparing pruning strategies at pre-retrieval,
post-retrieval, and pre-synthesis stages. Across
lightweight heuristic criteria, LLM-based prun-
ing, and an exploratory learned controller, we
find that pruning effectiveness depends strongly
onwherepruning is applied: early pruning
yields the largest end-to-end savings, while
later pruning mainly refines the final synthe-
sis context. Lightweight heuristics reduce to-
ken usage by up to 73% while approximately
preserving judged

evidence.excerpt:
Problem
At each pruning point, the system decides whether
candidate x contributes sufficient marginal value
to retain, given query Q and accumulated context
Ct: atPre-Retrieval, x is a subquery s∈ S; at
Post-RetrievalandPre-Synthesis, x is a context
item c. We formalize this through a unified scor-
ing function V(x|C t, Q), retaining x if its score
exceeds a stage-specific threshold ( τpre, τpost, or
τsyn). Because relevance, novelty, diversity, and
coverage may matter differently at different stages,
selecting the right instantiation of V motivates the
cross-stage comparison in Section 5. Algorithm 1
shows the full pipeline.

evidence.excerpt:
Our experiments are built on theGPT-Researcher
framework, which performs multi-step query de-
composition, retrieval, aggregation, and report
generation. The baseline is the standardGPT-
Researcherpipelinewithout any explicit pruning
policy, including the framework's default late-stage
context trimming before synthesis. All pruning
variants are implemented on top of the same under-
lying search policy, and where applicable, we reuse
cached subqueries and retrieved evidence across
runs, so observed differences are attributable to
pruning decisions under this fixed execution frame-
work. This design isolates the effect of pruning
stage and scoring rule, but does not fully separate
adaptive pruning from a static reduction in search
budget; a matched-budget shallow-search baseline
is therefore an important control for future work.

evidence.excerpt:
We evaluate methods along four dimensions:qual-
ity,relevance,faithfulness/source grounding, and
efficiency.
• Quality(§ A.2): Measured with a fixed rubric-
based LLM judge applied uniformly across all
methods. Because absolute rubric scores can
shift across judges, we interpret these values pri-
marily asrelative comparisons under a fixed in-
dependent judge. Appendix Table 4 reports a
judge-sensitivity analysis.
• Relevance(§ A.2): KPR+KPC (Key Point Recall
+ Key Point Contradiction), measuring coverage
of key informational points from ground-truth
documents while penalizing conflicting state-
ments.
• Source grounding(§ A.2): Citation Recall (Cit.),
an evidence-retention proxy measuring the frac-
tion of report claims linked to a retrievable source.
This metric does not by itself establish factual
correctness.
• Efficiency(§ A.3): Node count (Nodes), total
token cost in thousands

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Objective token, node, and runtime accounting, reference-document KPR+KPC, citation recall, and supplementary RACE-style cross-benchmark results corroborate the efficiency and coverage trade-offs independently of the rubric judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by a fixed rubric-based LLM judge, automated KPR+KPC against reference documents, citation recall, and objective token, node, and runtime measurements.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pruning decisions are made by fixed heuristic scoring rules, lexical proxies, prompt-based LLM gating, or an offline learned controller trained on submodular-family execution logs; no end-to-end tuning against the reported quality metrics is described.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that early post-retrieval pruning generates the bulk of token savings while pre-synthesis primarily refines quality are solidly supported by detailed stage-wise logging and token/node accounting.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation across 100 benchmark queries from DeepResearchGym measures objective efficiency metrics (node count, token cost, wall-clock time) alongside report quality, key point recall/contradiction, and citation recall, complemented by supplementary runs on DeepResearch Bench.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Objective token counts, node tracking, runtime profiling, reference-document key point recall (KPR+KPC), and cross-benchmark RACE evaluations corroborate the efficiency and coverage trade-offs independently of the LLM rubric judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Final pipeline outputs are evaluated using an independent LLM rubric judge, automated KPR+KPC key point coverage against reference documents, citation recall, and exact token/runtime measurements.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pruning decisions use fixed heuristic scoring rules, rule-based embedding metrics, prompt-based LLM gating, or offline learned controllers without end-to-end policy tuning on the evaluation metrics.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently report the lack of a matched-budget shallow-search baseline, sensitivity of absolute rubric scores across LLM judges, and variance across benchmarks.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology systematically compares heuristic criteria (MMR, centroid drift, geometric residual novelty, submodular coverage, DPP), lexical variants, LLM prompting, and learned gating on top of a consistent GPT-Researcher baseline.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper presents a well-structured, reproducible, and thorough empirical investigation of context pruning in multi-step agent architectures with balanced claims and rigorous token and runtime profiling.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript formulates and empirically evaluates stage-aware marginal-value pruning across pre-retrieval, post-retrieval, and pre-synthesis stages in a multi-step deep research agent pipeline.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper presents a well-structured, reproducible, and thorough empirical investigation of context pruning in multi-step agent architectures with balanced claims and rigorous token and runtime profiling.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently report the lack of a matched-budget shallow-search baseline, sensitivity of absolute rubric scores across LLM judges, and variance across benchmarks.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

relation_to_agentic_memory.value: Studies agents that perform or evaluate multi-step research workflows

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to autonomous/deep research workflows based on screening evidence.
